prompt: Change to passive with <have something done>
source: A professional cleaned our carpets.
correct: We had our carpets cleaned.
explanation: Causative <have something done>: subject + <had> + object + past participle.

prompt: Change to passive with <get something done>
source: A stylist cut her hair yesterday.
correct: She got her hair cut yesterday.
explanation: Informal causative: <get> + object + past participle.

prompt: Change to passive using present continuous
source: They are renovating the old library.
correct: The old library is being renovated.
explanation: Present continuous passive: subject + <is/are being> + past participle.

prompt: Change to passive using past continuous
source: Workers were repairing the road when I arrived.
correct: The road was being repaired when I arrived.
explanation: Past continuous passive: subject + <was/were being> + past participle.

prompt: Change to passive using present perfect
source: Someone has stolen my laptop.
correct: My laptop has been stolen.
explanation: Present perfect passive: subject + <has/have been> + past participle.

prompt: Change to passive using future
source: They will announce the results tomorrow.
correct: The results will be announced tomorrow.
explanation: Future passive: subject + <will be> + past participle.

prompt: Change to passive with modal
source: You must submit the application before Friday.
correct: The application must be submitted before Friday.
explanation: Modal passive: subject + modal + <be> + past participle.

prompt: Change to passive using <is expected to>
source: People expect that the prices will rise.
correct: Prices are expected to rise.
It is expected that prices will rise.
It's expected that prices will rise.
explanation: Impersonal passive: subject + <is expected to> + infinitive.

prompt: Change to passive with <is reported to>
source: Journalists report that the CEO has resigned.
correct: The CEO is reported to have resigned.
It is reported that the CEO has resigned.
It's reported that the CEO has resigned.
explanation: Impersonal passive with past reference: subject + <is reported to have> + past participle.

prompt: Change to active voice
source: The proposal was rejected by the committee.
correct: The committee rejected the proposal.
explanation: Active voice: agent becomes subject + verb in active form + object.

prompt: Change to passive with double object
source: They offered me a job.
correct: I was offered a job.
A job was offered to me.
hint: Double-object verbs allow two passive forms
explanation: With double-object verbs (offer, give, tell), either object can become the passive subject.

prompt: Change to passive with <need + gerund>
source: Someone needs to repair the roof.
correct: The roof needs repairing.
The roof needs to be repaired.
explanation: <Need + gerund> is a passive-meaning construction: <needs repairing> = <needs to be repaired>.

prompt: Change to passive using <is supposed to>
source: People say you should arrive 15 minutes early.
correct: You are supposed to arrive 15 minutes early.
You're supposed to arrive 15 minutes early.
explanation: <Be supposed to> expresses what is expected, often from external norms or rules.

prompt: Change to causative <have> in present
source: A dentist checks my teeth every six months.
correct: I have my teeth checked every six months.
explanation: Present causative: subject + <have> + object + past participle.

prompt: Change to causative <get> in future
source: A photographer will take our family portrait.
correct: We're going to get our family portrait taken.
We will get our family portrait taken.
explanation: Future causative with <get>: subject + <will get/be going to get> + object + past participle.

prompt: Change to passive with <is known to>
source: Everyone knows that she is an excellent musician.
correct: She is known to be an excellent musician.
It is known that she is an excellent musician.
explanation: Impersonal passive: subject + <is known to> + infinitive.

prompt: Change to passive with <is considered to be>
source: Most people consider this the best restaurant in town.
correct: This is considered to be the best restaurant in town.
This is considered the best restaurant in town.
explanation: Impersonal passive: subject + <is considered (to be)> + complement.

prompt: Change to active voice with agent
source: The windows are cleaned by a professional team every week.
correct: A professional team cleans the windows every week.
explanation: Active: agent becomes subject, verb in active form, object.

prompt: Change to passive with infinitive
source: They expect the company to announce the merger.
correct: The company is expected to announce the merger.
explanation: Complex passive: subject + <is expected to> + infinitive.

prompt: Change to causative <have> in past
source: An electrician installed new wiring in our house.
correct: We had new wiring installed in our house.
explanation: Past causative: subject + <had> + object + past participle.

prompt: Change to passive with <is thought to>
source: Scientists think that this species is endangered.
correct: This species is thought to be endangered.
It is thought that this species is endangered.
explanation: Impersonal passive: subject + <is thought to> + infinitive.

prompt: Change to passive with <is alleged to have>
source: Witnesses allege that the driver ran the red light.
correct: The driver is alleged to have run the red light.
It is alleged that the driver ran the red light.
explanation: Impersonal passive with past reference: <is alleged to have> + past participle.

prompt: Change to active voice
source: The new policy has been approved by the board.
correct: The board has approved the new policy.
explanation: Active present perfect: agent + <has/have> + past participle + object.

prompt: Change to passive with <want + object + past participle>
source: I want someone to deliver the package before noon.
correct: I want the package delivered before noon.
explanation: <Want + object + past participle> is an informal way to express desired action by others.

prompt: Change to passive using <it + passive + that clause>
source: Researchers have shown that exercise improves memory.
correct: It has been shown that exercise improves memory.
explanation: Impersonal passive: <It has been shown/proven/demonstrated that> + clause.
